children: The US' headquartered SLB and Paris-based Viridien will soon join Egypt in a new operation to hunt for gas in the Eastern Mediterranean as the third largest Arab economy strives to offset a decline in its gas output and reserves.

Phase 1 of an ambitious offshore gas exploration programme covers an area of around 18,000 square kilometres (sq km) and involves the deployment of the advanced subsea-bottom seismic (OBN) technology.

Egypt’s Minister of Petroleum and Mineral Resources Karim Badawi said the operation, which starts within two weeks, aims to enhance natural gas exploration opportunities and provide more accurate geological data, which will support attracting new investments and accelerating exploration and production decisions.

“The project represents a key element in developing exploration activities in Egypt by employing the latest global technologies in data collection and analysis. This will contribute to a better understanding of subsea geological structures, identify the most attractive areas for natural gas exploration, and open new horizons for international companies to inject more investments into exploration and production activities,” he said in statements published on the ministry’s website.

The project is being implemented by the Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Company (EGAS), in cooperation with a SLB-Viridien consortium, as part of an integrated seismic survey programme in Egyptian waters in the Eastern Mediterranean.

The program aims to cover a total area of 95,000 sq km, providing an extensive database to support efforts to assess and maximise the utilisation of undiscovered hydrocarbon resources, the statement said.
(Writing by N Saeed; Editing by Anoop Menon)

title: Egypt to hunt for gas in 18,000 sq km survey in Mediterranean
